headline: HSC and equivalent exam results published today for over 1.27 million students
summary: The results for over 1.27 million students who took the HSC and equivalent exams are being announced today. Students can check their scores online, via SMS, or through their institutions.
details: The wait is over for more than 1.27 million students who sat for the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations, with results set to be published today, Saturday. Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce the results at 11 AM at the conference room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division.

Students will be able to check their results through their educational institutions, online portals, or SMS after the official announcement. Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chief of the Inter-Board Coordination Committee, confirmed that preparations were nearing completion on Friday evening.

He noted that if the Prime Minister consents, the results would first be handed over to him, followed by a briefing. A total of 1,270,583 students participated in this year's HSC and equivalent examinations, which began on July 2 at 2,697 centres across the country.

The average pass rate across the nine general education boards, the Madrasa Education Board, and the Technical Education Board stood at 58.83 percent under the interim government. In 2024, the pass rate was 77.78 percent, though Akhtaruzzaman declined to speculate on this year's expected pass rate.

With the results due today, students are experiencing a mix of anticipation and apprehension, with many particularly worried about their performance in English. Labait Islam, a commerce student from Gazipur Metropolitan College, expressed relief if his results were "at least respectable."

Md Limon Islam, a humanities student from Dinajpur, also shared mixed emotions, believing he performed well in other subjects' multiple-choice questions. Shal Mrong, a science student from Dhaka, raised concerns about errors in some Physics and Chemistry question papers, hoping marks would be awarded for them.

Parents are also waiting anxiously to find out their children's fate. Dhaka resident Deepika, for instance, voiced her worry about her son's performance, especially as she hadn't seen him study much during the examination period.

Students and educational institutions can access the results through the education boards' websites: https://eduboardresults.gov.bd and https://educationboardresults.gov.bd. Institutions can download their results by visiting the "Result" section and entering their education board and EIIN.

Examinees can also receive their results via SMS from any mobile phone. To do so, type "HSC<space>three-letter code of the respective education board<space>roll number<space>examination year" and send the message to 16140.

Students dissatisfied with their results will have the opportunity to apply for re-checking of their answer scripts from November 1 to November 7. Applications must be submitted online through https://rescrutiny.eduboardresults.gov.bd, with a fee of Tk 150 for each subject.

Payments for re-scrutiny can be made through various mobile financial services like bKash, Nagad, DBBL, Rocket, Upay, or Sonali Bank's payment service. Students who fail this year's examinations will have the chance to retake them within two months of the results' publication, as per an earlier education ministry announcement.

headline_marked: [[Vegetable prices fall by over half]] in Dhaka markets as early-winter supply increases, bringing relief to buyers.
headline: Vegetable prices fall by over half in Dhaka markets as early-winter supply increases, bringing relief to buyers.
summary: Consumers in Dhaka are experiencing significant relief as prices for most early-winter vegetables have dropped by more than 50% in the past two weeks due to increased supply.
details: Prices of most vegetables have fallen significantly in Dhaka kitchen markets, with some dropping by more than half over the past two weeks. This relief for buyers comes as supplies of early-winter produce have increased across the city.

For instance, beans that were Tk 140-160 per kg are now Tk 50-80 per kg. Cauliflower and cabbage, previously Tk 60-80 each, are now available for Tk 30-60. Radish prices have also seen a substantial decrease.

Shoppers like Ranu Begum and Monjurul Islam expressed satisfaction, noting they can now afford larger quantities of seasonal produce. They had previously been unable to buy these vegetables due to high prices earlier in the season.
However, not all vegetables have followed this trend. Tomatoes and new potatoes continue to be relatively expensive, still selling for more than Tk 150 per kg in various markets.

Wholesale traders at Karwan Bazar confirm the increased supply, with one stating that supply currently exceeds demand. This situation makes it challenging for traders to make a significant profit despite the higher volume.
caption:
Dhaka residents rejoice as vegetable prices plummet by over 50% in local markets. Early-winter produce floods the market, offering much-needed relief to household budgets.

Prices of most vegetables have fallen significantly in Dhaka kitchen markets, with some dropping by more than half over the past two weeks. This relief for buyers comes as supplies of early-winter produce have increased across the city.

For instance, beans that were Tk 140-160 per kg are now Tk 50-80 per kg. Cauliflower and cabbage, previously Tk 60-80 each, are now available for Tk 30-60. Radish prices have also seen a substantial decrease.

Shoppers like Ranu Begum and Monjurul Islam expressed satisfaction, noting they can now afford larger quantities of seasonal produce. They had previously been unable to buy these vegetables due to high prices earlier in the season.

However, not all vegetables have followed this trend. Tomatoes and new potatoes continue to be relatively expensive, still selling for more than Tk 150 per kg in various markets.

Wholesale traders at Karwan Bazar confirm the increased supply, with one stating that supply currently exceeds demand. This situation makes it challenging for traders to make a significant profit despite the higher volume.
